A pile of filings as the tables an analysis reads

Source: R/xbrl_accounts.R
xbrl_accounts.Rd

Takes the fact table from read_xbrl() and divides it: who the company is, where it is, how the report was audited, what its statements say, what its fixed asset note shows, whether any of it adds up, and what management wrote. One named list of tibbles, every one of them opening with the same key, so that moving between them needs no looking.

Usage

xbrl_accounts(
  x,
  what = NULL,
  basis = c("parent", "consolidated"),
  persons = FALSE,
  taxonomy = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A tibble from read_xbrl().

what

Which tables to build. Any of "company", "audit", "location", "checks", "income_statement", "balance", "cash_flow", "movements" and "prose"; all nine by default.

basis

"parent" (default) or "consolidated", for the statements and the note. An untagged figure is the parent's – see add_taxonomy().

persons

Include the names of the auditor, the boards and the chairman in audit. Personal data, so off by default – see xbrl_company().

taxonomy

Passed to xbrl_lines(). NULL uses the packaged tables.

Value

A list of tibbles of class cvrr_accounts, named by what and in that order. The filings that could not be read are carried through in attr(a, "failed").

The key comes first, and is the same everywhere

cvr, name, period_start, period_end, in that order, at the front of every table, and file at the back of it – the key is what a reader joins and groups on, and the file name is what a figure is traced back to. name is repeated rather than left to a join: R keeps one copy of each distinct string and a pointer per row, so 127,000 balance sheet lines cost about a megabyte for never having to fetch a company's name in order to read its figures.

Why nine tables and not one

The company row is 40 columns wide and they answer different questions. development runs to 486 characters in the median filing, so keeping the prose beside the accounting class means every glance at the class drags a paragraph with it. And the verdicts are not attributes of a company at all; they are what the checks concluded about one filing.

company

Who this is: legal form, when it was founded, accounting class, employees, currency.

location

Where it is: street, postcode, city, country and the registered office it states.

audit

How the report came to be, and how far to trust its tagging: who audited it and with what opinion, who submitted it, when it was approved, and which tool wrote the XBRL. With persons, the names that signed it.

checks

What the checks concluded, one row per filing.

income_statement

One row per line, in statement order, as reported. See xbrl_lines().

balance

One row per line, with the lines the filer left out derived and marked in source. See xbrl_lines().

cash_flow

One row per line of the cash flow statement, as reported. Class B may leave the statement out, and a parent company that presents group accounts usually has one only on basis = "consolidated". See check_cashflow().

movements

The fixed asset note, one row per movement per asset class. See xbrl_movements().

prose

What management wrote: the activity, the year's development, events after the reporting period, mortgages and contingent liabilities.

what builds only the tables named, and skips the work they do not need: the checks are the expensive part, and what = "company" still runs them because that row reports their verdicts, while what = "location" runs none of them.

Whether it adds up

income_statement, balance and cash_flow carry reconciled on every row, so the commonest filter – give me only the lines that add up – needs no join. movements carries four verdicts of its own. And checks gathers the per-filing conclusions in one place, at the grain the question is asked:

  • balance_reconciled – the balance sheet's debit side equals its credit side, from check_statement().

  • income_reconciled – no step of the income statement's cascade is left unexplained, from check_cascade().

  • cashflow_reconciled – the activities sum to the change in cash, the change rolls the cash forward, and the closing cash is the balance sheet's, from check_cashflow().

  • cashflow_debt_backed – every krone the cash flow statement says was borrowed shows up as long-term debt in the balance sheet. It is FALSE for Greenland Airports' 2025 group accounts, whose internal arithmetic is perfect, and that is why it is a column of its own.

  • movements_reconciled – every block of the fixed asset note that could be checked rolls forward.

  • movements_cover – the notes together account for the fixed assets the balance sheet carries.

They are six columns and never one verdict, because a filing can pass any of them and fail the rest: a balance sheet that closes says nothing about whether the income statement does, and a fixed asset schedule that rolls forward perfectly for land and buildings says nothing about the machinery it never mentions. NA means there was nothing of that kind to check, which is not the same as failing.

Each is a summary of something you can go and look at: check_cascade() on one filing's facts gives the income statement's steps one row each, and movements gives the note's blocks one row per movement.

See also

read_xbrl() for what goes in, xbrl_lines(), xbrl_company() and xbrl_movements() for the tables one at a time, check_cascade(), check_statement() and check_cashflow() for the detail behind reconciled.

Other taxonomy: add_taxonomy(), check_breakdown(), check_cascade(), check_cashflow(), check_continuity(), check_inclusion(), check_movement(), check_statement(), read_taxonomy(), xbrl_company(), xbrl_fill(), xbrl_lines(), xbrl_movements(), xbrl_note_tables(), xbrl_panel(), xbrl_period(), xbrl_ratios(), xbrl_report(), xbrl_report_data(), xbrl_resolve(), xbrl_robustness(), xbrl_screen(), xbrl_standardise(), xbrl_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl")
a <- xbrl_accounts(x)
a

a$balance
subset(a$income_statement, reconciled)

# the tables join on the key they share
merge(a$checks, a$audit)

# just the one table, and only the work it needs
xbrl_accounts(x, what = "company")
} # }
